[[Image:Julia set (indigo).png|thumb|A [[Julia set]], a fractal related to the [[Mandelbrot set]]]]
[[Image:Animated fractal mountain.gif|right|thumb|200px|A fractal that models the surface of a mountain (animation)]]

In [[mathematics]], the '''Hutchinson metric''', otherwise known as the '''Kantorovich metric''', is a [[function (mathematics)|function]] which [[metric (mathematics)|measures]] "the discrepancy between two [[image]]s for use in [[fractal]] [[image processing]]" and "can also be applied to describe the similarity between [[DNA]] sequences expressed as real or complex [[genomic]] signals".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Drakopoulos |first1=V. |last2=Nikolaou |first2=N. P. |title=Efficient computation of the Hutchinson metric between digitized images |journal=IEEE Transactions on Image Processing |volume=13 |issue=12 |pages=1581–1588 |date=December 2004 |doi=10.1109/tip.2004.837550|pmid=15575153 |bibcode=2004ITIP...13.1581D }}</ref><ref>[http://isis.pub.ro/iafa2003/files/3-5.pdf Hutchinson Metric in Fractal DNA Analysis -- a Neural Network Approach] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110818165407/http://isis.pub.ro/iafa2003/files/3-5.pdf |date=August 18, 2011 }}</ref>

==Formal definition==
Consider only [[empty set|nonempty]], [[compact space|compact]], and finite [[metric space]]s. For such a space <math>X </math>, let <math>P(X)</math> denote the space of [[Borel measure|Borel]] [[probability measure]]s on <math>X</math>, with

:<math>\delta : X \rightarrow P(X)</math>

the embedding associating to <math>x \in X</math> the point measure <math>\delta_x</math>. The support <math>|\mu|</math> of a measure  in <math>P(X)</math> is the smallest [[closed subset]] of measure 1.

If  <math>f : X_1 \rightarrow X_2</math> is [[Borel measure|Borel measurable]] then the induced map

:<math>f_* : P(X_1) \rightarrow P(X_2)</math>

associates to <math>\mu</math> the measure <math>f_*(\mu)</math> defined by

:<math>f_*(\mu)(B)= \mu(f^{-1}(B))</math>

for all <math>B</math> Borel in <math>X_2 </math>.

Then the '''Hutchinson metric''' is given by

:<math>d(\mu_1,\mu_2) = \sup \left\lbrace \int u(x) \, \mu_1(dx) - \int u(x) \, \mu_2(dx) \right\rbrace</math>

where the <math>\sup</math> is taken over all [[real number|real]]-valued functions <math>u</math> with [[Lipschitz constant]] <math>\le\!1.</math>

Then <math>\delta</math> is an [[isometric embedding]] of <math>X</math> into <math>P(X)</math>, and if <math>f : X_1 \rightarrow X_2</math> is Lipschitz then <math>f_* : P(X_1) \rightarrow P(X_2)</math> is Lipschitz with the same Lipschitz constant.<ref>[https://www.jstor.org/stable/117923 "Invariant Measures for Set-Valued Dynamical Systems"] Walter Miller; Ethan Akin ''Transactions of the American Mathematical Society'', Vol. 351, No. 3. (March 1999), pp. 1203–1225]</ref>
